_doc: Revert-verify mutants for requirement 656bd2d9-458d-4b81-8ec3-49318b134e40 (ticket eb9d6d2c, branch feat/apply-input-schema-preflight) — `findInputSchemaViolation`, the pre-flight that enforces a command's declared `exocmd__Grounding_inputSchema`. Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout (both absolute). Guards enumerated per integration-test-revert-verify §A8 from `git diff -U0` of GroundingExecutor.ts: the two refusals (M1 undeclared key, M2 required key), the transitive step walk (M3), each of the four declared SOURCES that make the required refusal fail-open (M4 labelTemplate, M5 omitLabel, M6 the schema's own defaultValue, M7 propertyDefault, M8 inheritanceRule), the engine-reserved key set (M9), the blank-is-absent rule (M10), the `label`-is-not-covered-by-a-propertyDefault boundary (M11) and the no-schema early return (M12). Every `expect` is the MEASURED red set, never the predicted one (§A97 — a BROKEN mutant is the absence of a measurement, not a measurement); the prediction written before the run is quoted verbatim in each `_note`. ⛤ COMPANION SPECS, both load-bearing: `input-schema-656bd2d9.neighbour-gate.spec.json` proves the PRE-EXISTING `findMissingInput` type-gate is still alive after this change (integration-test-revert-verify §A7 — adding a branch must not silently retire the neighbouring guard), and `packages/cli/tests/integration/input-schema-656bd2d9.wiring.spec.json` proves the pre-flight is actually WIRED into `apply` on BOTH paths rather than merely correct in isolation. ⛔ Assetspace crossing carries NO mutant here, and not by oversight: `GroundingDefinition.steps` is typed `readonly GroundingDefinition[]`, i.e. this function receives steps ALREADY RESOLVED by CommandResolver, so no input to it can distinguish a step living in another assetspace from a local one — a mutant would be measuring the resolver, which has its own suites.

M1_undeclared_key_check_removed._note: The loop that refuses a key the schema does not declare is gone; an unknown key flows to the frontmatter write again. Predicted A3 A15.

M2_required_check_removed._note: The required-key refusal is gone; a call with no label degrades to "Untitled" exactly as before the requirement. Predicted A1 A13 A14.

M3_step_walk_removed._note: The source lookup stops at the top node. This is the shape that would refuse the LIVE composite bab33aac, whose labelTemplate sits on its first step. Predicted A6 A7.

M4_label_template_not_a_source._note: labelTemplate stops counting as a declared source — the naive `required`-only check that would refuse 4 live commands outright plus the composite. Predicted A5 A6 A7; MEASURED A5 A6 A7 A9. ⛔ The divergence is mine, not the axis': I predicted from the mutant's THEME (it touches the label source) instead of from what A9 ASSERTS (§A44) — A9's fixture covers its required `label` WITH a labelTemplate so that the axis isolates the schema `defaultValue`, so removing that source reddens it too. The extra red is correct and is kept.

M5_omit_label_not_a_source._note: omitLabel stops counting: a class whose display name is derived at render time would be refused for the label it deliberately omits. Predicted A8.

M6_schema_default_ignored._note: A required field carrying the schema's own defaultValue is refused anyway. Predicted A9.

M7_property_default_not_a_source._note: A propertyDefault writing the required property stops excusing it. Predicted A10.

M8_inheritance_rule_not_a_source._note: An inheritanceRule writing the required property stops excusing it. Predicted A11.

M9_engine_reserved_set_emptied._note: `body` / `plannedDate` become undeclared keys, so a legitimate call carrying them is refused. Type-preserving: the Set still exists and is still consulted. Predicted A12.

M10_blank_counts_as_supplied._note: A whitespace-only value satisfies the contract again and the call lands on "Untitled" — the degradation the requirement removes, re-entered through the back door. Predicted A13.
M10_blank_counts_as_supplied.from:
const isSupplied = (v: unknown): boolean =>
    v !== undefined &&
    v !== null &&
    !(typeof v === "string" && v.trim().length === 0);
M10_blank_counts_as_supplied.to:
const isSupplied = (v: unknown): boolean =>
    v !== undefined && v !== null;

M11_property_default_may_excuse_label._note: Drops the `key !== "label"` conjunct so a propertyDefault could excuse the required `label` INPUT. Predicted A14; MEASURED **NO reds**, and that is reported rather than hidden (§A35 — a guard whose removal changes no reachable outcome is defensive, not load-bearing; §A55 — name the non-coverage with a number instead of an implied level). WHY it cannot redden, measured not assumed: the source lookup compares `canonicalYamlKey(<schema key>)` with `canonicalYamlKey(<property name>)`, and `canonicalYamlKey("label")` = "label" while `canonicalYamlKey("exo__Asset_label")` = "exo__Asset_label" (the unprefixing whitelist covers `aliases`, not `label`) — so the two never compare equal with or without the conjunct. A fixture that DID redden it would need a propertyDefault literally named `label`, a form `resolvePropertyDefaults` cannot produce because it names a default by its property asset's label, i.e. the prefixed spelling. The conjunct stays because that non-equality lives in ANOTHER module (NoteToRDFConverter) and this file should not depend on it silently; A14 remains as a behavioural axis — it locks the OUTCOME (a Universal-Default-Template propertyDefault does not excuse the required label input), which is what production relies on. ⛤ The dependency is WATCHED, so the conjunct is not permanently asleep: `UNPREFIXED_ASSET_FIELDS` is {draft, pinned, aliases} and growing it reddens axes that already exist — packages/cli/tests/integration/canonical-key-single-source.integration.test.ts, and packages/cli/tests/unit/commands/create.test.ts states it verbatim ("add a fifth entry to `UNPREFIXED_ASSET_FIELDS` and the copy diverges"). Whoever adds `label` there is told by those tests; the ⛤-paragraph at the call site tells them what changes HERE when they do.

M12_empty_schema_no_longer_exempt._note: Only `undefined` short-circuits; a schema that declares zero properties now refuses every key. Type-preserving (the guard still narrows `fields`), unlike deleting the return outright, which would leave `fields.map` on a possibly-undefined value. Predicted A4.
